summary:
We developed an astronaut health monitoring system that processes physiological data, such as heart rate, stress levels, and physical activity, alongside environmental data, including radiation, pressure, and temperature.

The system identifies abnormal variations, assesses potential emergency situations, and alerts the mission team with the astronaut's name, location, and the reason for the alert. It also provides a personal monitoring dashboard that explains each metric and its current status.

Our main innovation is the combination of deterministic analysis and AI. Instead of relying solely on AI to interpret raw data, our system applies predefined rules to identify anomalies and understand their context before involving AI. For example, it considers recorded physical activity when evaluating an increase in heart rate.

This approach aims to provide more contextualized health assessments, support faster emergency response, and improve astronaut health monitoring during space missions.
details:
Project Overview

Our project is an astronaut health monitoring system designed to support crew health and safety during space missions. It collects and processes physiological data, such as heart rate (BPM), stress levels, and physical activity, alongside environmental information, including radiation, pressure, and temperature.

The system analyzes this information to identify abnormal variations and potentially dangerous situations. When an issue is detected, it generates an alert for the mission team, providing relevant context, including the astronaut's name, location, and the reason for the alert.

Astronauts also have access to a personal monitoring dashboard that displays their health metrics, explains their current status, and helps them understand changes in their condition. Additionally, the application includes an AI-powered Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) assistant that provides physical and mental health guidance based on NASA documentation.

How It Works

One of the main components is our analysis engine, developed in Rust. Rather than relying entirely on AI to interpret raw data, it uses deterministic rules, individual baselines, and variation analysis to identify unusual changes in an astronaut's condition.

The system also considers context when evaluating measurements. For example, an increase in heart rate may be expected after physical exercise. By considering recorded activities alongside physiological measurements, the engine can provide more meaningful assessments instead of treating every variation as an immediate warning.

The RAG assistant complements this process by retrieving relevant information from NASA documentation and using an AI language model to provide contextualized guidance.

Benefits and Intended Impact

Our goal is to improve astronaut health monitoring and support faster responses to potential emergencies. By combining continuous monitoring, contextual analysis, and accessible health information, the system aims to help astronauts better understand their condition while allowing mission teams to identify situations that may require attention.

This approach is particularly relevant to space missions, where medical resources are limited, environmental conditions are challenging, and timely access to reliable information is essential.

Technologies and Tools

The project was developed using:

  • Flutter and Dart: Cross-platform application and user interface.
  • Rust: Health data processing and deterministic analysis engine.
  • AI and RAG: Retrieval-based assistant for physical and mental health guidance.
  • NASA documentation: Reference material used to support the assistant's responses and the project's health-related knowledge base.

Creativity and Design Considerations

The main creative aspect of our solution is the combination of deterministic analysis and AI in a single monitoring system. Instead of asking an AI model to make every interpretation, we designed an analysis process that first evaluates measurements, individual patterns, and contextual information.

We considered the specific challenges of astronaut health monitoring, including individual physiological differences, environmental risks, the importance of identifying abnormal variations, and the need to communicate alerts clearly.

By bringing these elements together, our project aims to provide a more contextual and accessible approach to health monitoring in space.
